title: Qt: Get the BPF filter actually used in CompiledFilterOutput
description:
On Linux, at least, (and Windows with recent npcap) the compiled capture filter
for a live packet capture may use BPF extensions (e.g., when filtering
for VLAN, because what the kernel hands to libpcap may have the VLAN
tag removed and placed elsewhere.) There are also some capture filter
expressions that can be valid for a live capture but not when reading
from a saved file (e.g., the Linux kernel can support the ifindex
keyword on any live capture). See pcap_compile(3PCAP) for details.

The only way to get the actual BPF filter used is to call dumpcap with
the actual interface name (and any necessary link-layer type), instead
of compiling a generic filter for the link-layer type. Note that while
this can fail with permission errors due to lack of privileges, it
already failed in the same scenario with bad permissions - the
difference is that the lack of permissions earlier led to an error
message about an illegal "-1" link-layer type for "Unknown". Now the
error message is more accurate.

For the capture syntax worker that is called constantly whenever the
text changes (as opposed to when a button is clicked), for now
mark capture filters that use such expressions as unknown (yellow/
deprecated). It's not clear if we want to hold open a bunch of pcap_t
handles (or open them repeatedly, which might spawn UAC prompts on
Windows.) This will at least allow those filters to be compiled and used.

There's an `extcap_verify_capture_filter` function that `CaptureFilterSyntaxWorker::checkFilter` calls (but `CompiledFilterOutput` has never used.) That should presumably be used for extcaps, which dumpcap doesn't know about (and will report that the device doesn't exist.)

added 2 commits
  • 7d224b77 - 1 commit from branch wireshark:master
  • c47ae1ff - Qt: Get the BPF filter actually used in CompiledFilterOutput
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21025/diffs?diff_id=1468071280&start_sha=13c0291cea6caa0b9f98f7415f0c6f2d695d2006)

"Work" in what sense? And "filters" in what sense - libpcap filter expressions, or (c)BPF programs? A *compiled* filter may only work on Linux if it uses the extensions, but the filter expression that compiles to that code if the target is "Linux kernel live capture" should work in either case.

`pcap_compile(3PCAP)` gives the example of the "ifindex" keyword, where the filter expression does not work without the extensions:

> For example,  the  ifindex  keyword  is valid for any live capture on Linux, but when reading packets from a savefile, regardless of the OS it  is  valid for DLT_LINUX_SLL2 only.

And indeed

```bash
$ ./run/dumpcap -d -i enp6s0 -f "ifindex 2"
Capturing on 'enp6s0'
(000) ld       [ifidx]
(001) jeq      #0x2             jt 2	jf 3
(002) ret      #262144
(003) ret      #0
```

works but right now the CaptureFilterSyntaxWorker says:

> ifindex not supported on Ethernet (not a live capture)

and the filter syntax worker turns red.
That different from the `vlan` filters, where the Linux BPF extensions are necessary to produce the proper bytecode but the filter expression is valid either way.

As written that's obviously a bit of a silly example, but you could write a more complicated filter with `or` and other things in it that captures X on one ifindex and Y on another, and do so without using the "any" interface.
`outbound` and `inbound` do the same thing, and is I think considerably more useful (and not supported right now.)

```bash
$ ./run/dumpcap -d -i enp6s0 -f "inbound"
Capturing on 'enp6s0'
(000) ldh      [type]
(001) jeq      #0x4             jt 2	jf 3
(002) ret      #0
(003) ret      #262144
```

but can't be used at all from Wireshark right now because it turns the syntax checker red as "not a live capture".

> the "ifindex" keyword, where the filter expression does not work without the extensions:

It's also not useful except on a capture on multiple interfaces, so, while it may work on a live capture on something other than the "any" device, it either matches all packets or matches no packets.

In capture files, it works only on `LINKTYPE_LINUX_SLL{2}` link-layer types, as those are the only ones that provide an interface index (a pcapng interface ID doesn't count).

libpcap could fake it, on any platform where you can get the ifindex of a given interface with an ioctl or other such call (given the number of SNMP agents out there that need ifindices, I suspect that's most if no all platforms), by, for live captures on anything other than the "any" device, getting the ifindex for the interface at compile time and generating either "always matches" or "never matches". We can't do that for non-`LINKTYPE_LINUX_SLL{2}` capture files unless we have an IDB option giving the ifindex.

For inbound and outbound, libpcap, if it wrote pcapng, could put the relevant information in the EPB flags (#12329, which strikes me as mostly a libpcap issue at this point.) Having the capture filter would still be useful.

> For inbound and outbound, libpcap, if it wrote pcapng, could put the relevant information in the EPB flags (#12329,

That's my intent - see [libpcap issue #1321](https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/libpcap/issues/1321); I'll mention that explicitly there.

> which strikes me as mostly a libpcap issue at this point.)

Yes.

In particular, see [this comment on libpcap issue #1321](https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/libpcap/issues/1321#issuecomment-2157344291):

> EPBs for packets that indicate the interface on which the packet arrived, as well as providing various EPB options such as the flag word, so that packet direction, etc. can be provided.

I'll clarify that the "various EPB options" does *not* apply only to "any"-device captures.

commits_data.title: Qt: Get the BPF filter actually used in CompiledFilterOutput
commits_data.message:
Qt: Get the BPF filter actually used in CompiledFilterOutput

On Linux, at least, (and now Windows with recent npcap) the compiled
capture filter for a live packet capture may use BPF extensions (e.g.,
when filtering for VLAN, because what the kernel hands to libpcap may
have the VLAN tag removed and placed elsewhere.) There are also some
capture filter expressions that can be valid for a live capture but
not when reading from a saved file (e.g., the Linux kernel can support
the ifindex, inbound, and outbound keywords on any live capture).
See pcap_compile(3PCAP) for details.

The only way to get the actual BPF filter used is to call dumpcap with
the actual interface name (and any necessary link-layer type), instead
of compiling a generic filter for the link-layer type. Note that while
this can fail with permission errors due to lack of privileges, it
already failed in the same scenario with bad permissions - the
difference is that the lack of permissions earlier led to an error
message about an illegal "-1" link-layer type for "Unknown". Now the
error message is more accurate.

We can't do this for pipes, standard input, or extcaps, which
aren't devices that dumpcap knows about.

For the capture syntax worker that is called constantly whenever the
text changes (as opposed to when a button is clicked), for now
mark capture filters that use such expressions as unknown (yellow/
deprecated). It's not clear if we want to hold open a bunch of pcap_t
handles (or open them repeatedly, which might spawn UAC prompts on
Windows.) That will at least allow filters with those keywords to be
compiled, and to be used in a capture.

The long term solution is probably something like holding dumpcap open
as a child process and sending messages back and forth, so it only has
to open devices once.
